learning_outcomes.text: Understands the basic concepts of thermodynamics and energy transformations. Applies the zeroth law of thermodynamics to the relationship between temperature and thermal equilibrium.
Understands the properties of pure substances. Relates phase change to material properties. Identifies and calculates state quantities.
Applies the relationships between pressure, temperature, and specific volume for gases. Determines properties using the ideal gas equation and calculates the work done during state changes.

Applies the First Law of Thermodynamics to cycles, closed and open systems, and performs system analysis. Calculates heat and work interactions as well as mass and energy balances. Determines heat and work relations for cycles in closed and open systems.
Defines the Second Law of Thermodynamics, applies it to a cycle and heat pumps, and calculates cycle efficiency and coefficients of performance.
Defines and determines entropy and entropy change. Demonstrates the principle of entropy and the increase of entropy, and applies it to thermodynamic systems

syllabus_topics: Definition and Scope of Thermodynamics, System, Surroundings, Boundary, Open and Closed Systems, and Control Volume
Pressure, Temperature, Specific Volume, Density, Specific Weight, and Thermodynamic Equilibrium
Energy Analysis of Closed Systems – Applications
Mass and Energy Analysis of Control Volumes
Energy Analysis of Control Volumes – Applications
Reversible and Irreversible Processes, Carnot Principles, the Carnot Cycle, Thermal Efficiency of Heat Engines, and Coefficient of Performance
The Concept of Entropy, Entropy Change, and Entropy Generation
